palavras: hermes trismegistus, commonly known as the hermes hermes
resposta: Hermes Trismegistus, the three times greater, is a legendary figure, the fusion of the Greek god Hermes with the Egyptian Thoth. There's no proof that he ever existed as a person. The texts attributed to him, the Corpus Hermeticum, were written in Greek in Roman Egypt around the second and third centuries.
aprofundar: In the Renaissance, Marsilio Ficino translated the Corpus in 1463 thinking it was older than Moses. In 1614, Isaac Casaubon showed by language that it was from the Christian era. Inner reading: Hermes is the messenger between the worlds, the mind that connects high and low. Practice: read the Emerald Tablet and think of a bridge between your inside and your outside.
camada3: To contemplate: perhaps Hermes never existed, and yet his image has guided seekers for centuries. Does a symbol have to be historical to be true on the inside?

resposta: Pythagoras of Samos lived in the sixth century B.C.E. and founded in Crotona, southern Italy, a community of study, dance, music, and discipline. He left nothing written; almost everything we know came from his disciples and much later authors.
aprofundar: The Pythagoreans taught that number is the essence of things and that the stars produce a harmony of the spheres. The theorem that bears his name was already known to the Babylonians. Inner reading: the order of the cosmos and the order of the soul correspond. Practice: end the day like the Pythagoreans, according to tradition, reviewing what you did, what you didn't do, and where you went wrong.
camada3: To contemplate: between chaos and order there is proportion. What proportion is missing in your life today between work and rest, talking and listening?

resposta: Heraclitus of Ephesus lived about 500 B.C. He taught that everything is changing, that opposites unite, and that there is a Logos, a reason that governs everything. Only fragments of his work remain.
aprofundar: Fragments known: one cannot step twice into the same river; the way up and down is one; the character of man is his destiny. He was called the Dark One because he spoke in riddles. Practice: today, when something changes against your will, say, the river is different, and so am I.
camada3: For contemplation: Heraclitus said that nature loves to hide. What's the truest thing about you that's still hidden?

palavras: i just know i don t know anything
resposta: Socrates of Athens died in 399 B.C.E., condemned to drink hemlock for corrupting youth and failing to honor the city's gods. He wrote nothing; we know him as Plato and Xenophon.
aprofundar: His method was to ask until the person saw the contradictions of one's own certainties: the maiutic, the birth of ideas. In Apology, he says that a life without examination is not worth living. The phrase I only know that I know nothing is a popular summary; Plato writes that he claimed to be wise only because he knew that he did not know. Practice: pick one certainty and give it three why's.
camada3: To contemplate: Socrates would rather die than stop asking. What question are you afraid to ask?

resposta: Plato, a disciple of Socrates, founded the Academy of Athens about 387 B.C.E. He taught that the world we see is a shadow of a world of eternal Ideas, and that the soul remembers the truth.
aprofundar: The Allegory of the Cave in Book Seven of the Republic sums it all up. For Plato, philosophy is born of awe and is a preparation for death, that is, a detachment from what passes. Practice: Today, in front of something beautiful, ask yourself, what greater beauty is this reflection of?
camada3: To contemplate: if the soul remembers, learning is remembering. What do you already know and forget? Say allegory of the cave.

resposta: Siddhartha Gautama, the Buddha, which means awakened, lived in northern India around the fifth century B.C. He taught the Four Noble Truths: there is suffering; it has a cause, attachment; it can cease; and there is a path, the Noble Eightfold Path.
aprofundar: The middle way avoids both excessive pleasure and mortification. The Dhammapada begins like this: the mind precedes all things. And teach: hatred never ceases by hatred; only by love does it cease. Beware: many Buddha quotes on the Internet are false. Practice: Watch your breathing for ten minutes.
camada3: To contemplate: Buddha told his disciples that teaching is like a raft, it's for crossing the river, not carrying on your back. What raft are you carrying without needing to?

resposta: Lao-tse, the old master, is the sage to whom the Tao Te Ching is attributed. According to legend, he left China riding a buffalo and wrote the book at the request of a border guard. Historians do not know whether he existed as a person; the book seems to have been compiled in the fourth century before Christ.
aprofundar: The central teaching: to live in harmony with the Tao, with simplicity, humility and effortless action. Chapter sixty-four: the journey of a thousand leagues begins beneath your feet. Practice: Do something today that's slower than usual, with full concentration.
camada3: To contemplate: the wise man, says the Tao, does not show himself and therefore shines. Where could you shine less to illuminate more? Say the Tao Te Ching.

resposta: Most historians, believers and nonbelievers, agree that Jesus of Nazareth existed, was a Jewish preacher from Galilee, and was crucified in Jerusalem under Pontius Pilate about 30 C.E. The center of his teaching is God's Kingdom and love for God and neighbor, even the enemy.
aprofundar: In the Sermon on the Mount, in Matthew five to seven: Blessed are the meek, the merciful, the pure in heart; pray in secret; do not lay up treasures on earth. He denounced those who laid heavy burdens on the shoulders of others and challenged the religious hypocrisy of his day. Practice: Choose a bliss and live it today.
camada3: To reflect: At Luke 17:21, the Kingdom of God is within you. If he's in, what needs to come out for him to show up?

resposta: Jalal ad-Din Rumi, Persian poet and Sufi master, lived from 1207 to 1273 in Konya, in modern-day Turkey. His encounter with the wandering mystic Shams of Tabriz turned him into a poet of divine love. His greatest work is the Masnavi.
aprofundar: The Masnavi opens with the reed flute that weeps the separation from the reedbed: the soul that yearns for its origin. His followers founded the Mevlevi order, the spinning dervishes. Beware: many of Rumi's phrases circulating on the Internet have been invented or heavily altered, and some erase their Islamic roots. Practice: Listen to a song in complete silence, with your eyes closed, as if it were a prayer.
camada3: To contemplate: Rumi called love the astrolabe of the mysteries of God. What in your life do you know just because you loved?

resposta: Master Eckhart, a German Dominican friar, lived from about 1260 to 1328. He was one of the greatest Christian mystics. Some of his phrases were condemned by Pope John XXII in 1329, after his death.
aprofundar: He spoke of the depths of the soul, where God gives birth to the Son, and of detachment, the Gelassenheit, letting go. A real phrase from a sermon: The eye with which I see God is the same eye with which God sees me. Practice: For five minutes, stop asking and just stay.
camada3: To contemplate: Eckhart prayed to God to rid him of God, that is, of the little images we make of him. What image of God do you need to let go?

resposta: Carl Gustav Jung, Swiss psychiatrist, lived from 1875 to 1961. He broke with Freud and created analytical psychology, with ideas like the collective unconscious, archetypes, shadow and individuation, the process of becoming whole.
aprofundar: Jung studied alchemy, gnosticism, myths and religions as maps of the soul. In a 1916 letter, he wrote: "He who looks outside dreams; he who looks within awakens". And in Alchemical Studies, no one becomes enlightened by imagining figures of light, but by making darkness conscious. Practice: Write down one dream a day for a week.
camada3: To contemplate: What you most criticize in others may be your shadow. Say shadow to go deeper.

palavras: the truth and a land without roads
a verdade e uma terra sem caminhos
resposta: Jiddu Krishnamurti, an Indian, lived from 1895 to 1986. He was created by the Theosophical Society to be the new teacher of the world, but in 1929 he dissolved the order created for him and said: truth is a pathless land.
aprofundar: He refused to be a guru and taught nonjudgmental observation, freedom from all spiritual authority, including his own. A famous phrase attributed to him, that it is not a sign of health to be adapted to a sick society, has no confirmed source in his works. Practice: observe a thought without condemning or justifying it.
camada3: To contemplate: he left the throne given to him so as not to imprison anyone. What authority, even spiritual, have you placed above your own observation?
